text:
For 40 minutes this was a goalies' game, and Anaheim was winning it on chances. Then the third period produced five goals, Seattle led three separate times, and the night ended with one more loss for a Ducks team that is now winless in four.

Anaheim owned the second period, 1.36 expected goals to 0.32, and Joey Daccord's stop on Nikita Nesterenko, a 37% look, kept it scoreless. Seattle broke through 2:51 into the third when Ben Meyers, an undrafted forward, converted a 6% chance. Cutter Gauthier answered 75 seconds later on a 2% snap shot. Colorado had ended his goal streak over the weekend, and he still came in chasing a scoring mark; he keeps finding ways onto the sheet. Vince Dunn's slap shot made it 2-1, Sam Colangelo tied it on a 2% chance with Stian Solberg picking up his first NHL point, and then Kaapo Kakko won it with 2:25 left. That goal moved Seattle from 52% to 90% to win.

Here is the frustrating part for Anaheim: the Ducks had the better even-strength chances (2.38 to 1.67) and deserved to win 61% of the replays of this game's shots. Seattle's 3.61 expected goals came mostly from a third period in which it piled up 2.75. Lukas Dostal gave up three goals on 21 shots, about one more than they deserved, while Daccord saved 0.57 more than expected on 26.

The context makes the skid sting more. Leo Carlsson left Saturday's game in Utah with an upper-body injury and is day-to-day, and Beckett Sennecke is on injured reserve. A team that leaned on its young core is playing without two of its centrepieces, and it showed in how hard Anaheim had to work for each goal.

For Seattle, it was a needed answer after a 4-3 loss to San Jose over the weekend, when Lane Lambert called the penalty kill "the elephant in the room," per Alison Lukan. The kill was not tested much here: Anaheim had two power plays and 0.18 expected goals on them.
headline: Kakko settles a wild third, Ducks' skid hits four
